init.title: Claim the engine lease
init.imperative: The worktree, the .agent-work directory, and this spine.json already exist by the time you load: your dispatcher (the Admiral for a delegated run, the human for an interactive one) stood them up per references/stand-up-work-area.md before handing you this spine path. You do not scaffold anything here -- claim the engine session lease on this spine so a resumed or duplicated parent cannot concurrently drive it: call the spine_lease MCP tool with action=claim, claimed_by=commander, worktree=. (add force=true and reason="resuming this run" if a stale prior lease blocks you) -- this is your own spine (the one this process's door is bound to), so the door needs no session id argument, it reads SPINE_SESSION from its own environment.

postconditions.statement: engine session lease claimed for this spine (commander owns the state)
postconditions.satisfied_by: Lease claimed via spine_lease action=claim, claimed_by=commander, worktree=.

context.title: Load baseline context
context.imperative: Read your inherited global doctrine (this skill's references/global-orchestrator.md and references/global-everyone.md), then the project deltas: docs/agents/ORCHESTRATOR_CONTEXT.md, docs/agents/GLOSSARY.md, docs/agents/engine-config.json. Where the repo carries no docs/agents/ overlay at all (e.g. a skill-source repo), substitute the closest repo doctrine you can find (README, CONTRIBUTING, top-level docs) and record the substitution — do not treat those paths as guaranteed to exist. Before you open any source file, resolve and read the map input: run python /home/tommy/.claude/skills/constellation-commander/scripts/map_orient.py orient --root /home/tommy/projects/569-w3-ci --work-id w3-ci. On RESOLVED, read the entrypoint it names and the packets, overlays and decision anchors it routes you to for the area the ask touches, and treat every later source read as confirming a frame the map already gave you rather than building one out of code. On DEGRADED, re-run the same command with --substitute PATH (what you read instead of a map — it is hash-pinned into the receipt) --unmapped TEXT (what stayed unmapped) --escalation TEXT (what you are escalating, and to whom), and get that on the record before any source read: degraded is a declared reading, never a licence to start from code. The tool probes a fixed fallback order — README.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, a docs/ index — and labels a substitute it found there as verified by the filesystem rather than merely asserted by you. This read is the map-first input the mission frame and plan are built from. Attest c1.
context.map_check_note: Why c2's deadline is worded as an ACT ('before you open any source file') rather than an artifact -- for whoever CHANGES this check, not for a run following the step. `current` never renders this field. A map-first imperative anchored to a late artifact does not bind at all: the gate plan is authored at the END of a long run, so a run that crawls source for fifty calls, reads the map afterwards, and writes an identical receipt has complied exactly (run #698: source at call 25, map at call 57). That is measured behaviour, not a hypothetical (epic-298/#307 measured the fix: map_before_src PRE-B 0/4 -> POST 4/4; see .agent-work/archive/2026-08-03-epic-298/ADMIRAL_LOG.md), and it is why the anchor lives at `context`, which precedes understand and plan. Ordering itself stays unverifiable from the receipt -- see this step's imperative and the report-only ordering audit, never this check. Gate-vs-report is a flag flip: appending --report-only turns this gate into a non-blocking report without rewiring the step.

plan.title: Author the gate plan
plan.imperative:
Map-first: BEFORE authoring execute.json, produce a mission frame from the map input the context step resolved, filling templates/MISSION_FRAME.template.md. Write it to .agent-work/w3-ci/MISSION_FRAME.md. Every anchor id the frame cites must resolve against the map inventory the context step committed to, or against the substitutes its receipt hash-pinned when context came back DEGRADED; c6 runs map_orient.py verify-frame over it.

For a trivial local/mechanical change where the map adds nothing, shrink or skip the frame and say so in its intent; then do both of these, or advance refuses: waive c6 (spine_evidence MCP tool, action=waive, task_id=plan, condition_id=c6, which=postconditions, authority=human, reason='...') AND attest c1 as skipped-as-trivial for the same reason.

For any low-confidence/stale/disputed map area the run depends on, alter the plan: add a scout/verification gate, or surface it to the human as a decision. Surface durable-structure choices as decision candidates per the skill's Decision candidates section rather than choosing alone.

Plan in this order, and do not reorder it — candidates, convergence, critic, execute.json.
  (1) Run plan-alternatives: N>=2 agents in parallel, each authoring one candidate GATE PLAN under one named distinct constraint, per references/design-it-twice-brief.md; write each to .agent-work/w3-ci/plan-candidate-<constraint>.md, kebab-case.
  (2) Converge to one recommendation; the human picks the winner or the hybrid. Record the comparison, the recommendation, the untaken roads, and the panel-vs-single choice in .agent-work/w3-ci/PLAN_ALTERNATIVES.md, filling references/design-it-twice-brief.md.
  (3) Run a cold plan critic over the converged candidate plan and the mission frame only, with no authoring context; write its findings to .agent-work/w3-ci/PLAN_CRITIC.md with a disposition on every finding, and have the human triage them.
  (4) Only then author the winner into execute.json — candidates you generate while attached to an incumbent are a justification, not a comparison. Author each gate as the smallest reasonable bite, with close criteria, required evidence, and an anchors block cut from the frame.
Run (1) and (3) by default; surface any skip as a named untaken road, with the panel-vs-single choice, at plan approval.

Before the plan freezes:
  - Ownership scope: every file and decision-class in the issue's stated file-ownership scope has its own gate, enumerated against the authored gates — a gate imperative that defers a decision as "handled elsewhere" is not that gate.
  - Verification green at every gate boundary: when the plan creates a new artifact family that a discovery/CI/test layer validates, the first gate touching that family ships the minimal valid artifact, a stub if that is enough, rather than opening a known-red window bridged by waivers.
  - Map entry point: every crew handoff names the map file(s) where that crew starts.

Get the human to approve the plan. In delegated mode, satisfy c3 (plan approved) by attaching a user-decision evidence item citing the launch order's frozen plan and scope -- via the spine_evidence MCP tool (action=attach, task_id=plan, evidence_type=user-decision, fields={cite: 'LAUNCH_ORDER:Mission'}); surface a plan-invalidating discovery to the Admiral rather than blocking on the human. See the commander skill's Delegated/autonomous mode.
plan.map_check_note: Why c6 is worded and placed the way it is -- for whoever CHANGES this check, not for a run following the step. Read it before editing c6 or its command; a run needs nothing here, and `current` never renders this field. WHAT IT IS. `map_orient.py verify-frame` is a REGRESSION FLOOR against map-IGNORING, not a fix for map-LATENESS. Its load-bearing refusals are the ones nothing else makes: an absent or empty frame REFUSES rather than vacuously passing, and a frame whose only citations are source paths is refused as cut from CODE. In RESOLVED mode every anchor must be a member of the map inventory the `context` step already committed to; in DEGRADED mode the frame must cite the substitutes that receipt hash-pinned. Either way the frame is compared against a prior declaration rather than a same-breath claim. WHAT THE MEASUREMENT MEANS, because the bare numbers mislead -- this note carries the ruling precisely so the next reader does not re-derive it and reach for --report-only. Against epic-298's baseline five runs the gate scored sensitivity 0/4 and specificity 0/1, and commander-304's ratified finding was ZERO DISCRIMINATING POWER against that population. Read that precisely: it is NOT 'the baseline happened to contain none of the mode this floor targets'. All four defective runs would have authored a CORRECT anchor-bearing frame from the map they had already read for confirmation, so the gate would have passed them while they were still defective -- 'the bypass is not a loophole someone might find, it is the measured behaviour'. The single firing was #716, whose correct answer was NON-ENGAGEMENT: a task where the map adds nothing. That firing is the trivial-change escape working as designed, not a defect, which is why c6 is waivable and why the imperative pairs that waiver with c1's skipped-as-trivial attestation. WHY IT SHIPS BLOCKING ANYWAY, ratified with both numbers in hand rather than in ignorance of them -- see .agent-work/archive/2026-08-03-epic-298/ADMIRAL_LOG.md, the 2026-08-02 RULING entries. The contract's genuinely new value is REPORTED DEGRADED MODE: in a repo with no map there was previously no contract at all -- silent crawl, no record -- and degraded is the COMMON case, most repos including this one. The floor's job is that map-ignoring cannot silently RETURN. It was never described as the answer to what was measured, and must not be: do not overclaim it, and never cite it as evidence that planning was map-first. THE RESCUE THAT WAS ALREADY TRIED AND FAILED. Pre-crawl expectations recorded in the receipt do not work: nothing the corpus owns can distinguish an expectation written before the crawl from one written after, and the only ordering evidence is the transcript. The ordering that actually matters is map-before-HYPOTHESIS, and the hypothesis forms during exploration, before any artifact exists. Demoting this gate therefore buys no better check; there is none available at this tier. DO NOT 'fix' the asymmetry (verify-orientation at context, verify-frame only here) by also running verify-frame at context: no frame exists at context -- the step runs before understand and plan -- so the only way to make it pass there is to let an ABSENT frame pass, which is the exact refusal the check is built on. If verify-frame ever has to be context-safe, give it a step-scoped mode; never a vacuous pass. Gate-vs-report is a flag flip: appending --report-only turns this gate into a non-blocking report without rewiring the step. Before reaching for it, note what the flip costs: it converts a tripwire carrying a recorded human waiver into a report nobody reads, which is the silent-crawl state this contract was built to end.

execute.title: Execute the plan
execute.imperative: Before entering this step: ensure context headroom (run a harness compaction command if one is exposed, else rely on harness auto-compaction — either is fine) and reload the constellation-commander skill into this context, confirming it is active; this satisfies p1. Then, before this step and before EACH detached dispatch, (re)write the crash-resume state note at .agent-work/w3-ci/STATE_NOTE.md (step · slug · next command · PID · expected artifact) from .agent-work/templates/STATE_NOTE.template.md, or the bundled templates/STATE_NOTE.template.md when the project has no .agent-work/templates/ overlay — the PID changes per detach, and the engine refuses to start execute until it is filled (precondition p2). Then drive execute.json gate by gate in this conversation using this skill's gate execution instructions. Dispatch subagents only for the implementer and reviewer tasks within each gate, and NEVER hand-launch a crew: run every implementer/reviewer dispatch through python /home/tommy/.claude/skills/constellation-commander/scripts/run_crew.py (foreground/blocking, durable registry, result-artifact verification). Before this step and before EACH crew dispatch, run python /home/tommy/.claude/skills/constellation-commander/scripts/recover_crews.py w3-ci and only launch when it reports no unresolved running/resumable/conflicting crew for that work-id/gate/role/worktree; recover (resume) or explicitly abandon/relaunch any it flags. Record completed outcomes, observed-vs-expected wave evidence, and classified discrepancies at .agent-work/w3-ci/REPLAN_INPUT.json as execution proceeds, in the exact fields of ../constellation-replan/templates/REPLAN_INPUT.template.json when this run is reshaping an epic's wave plan, or of ../constellation-replan/templates/RUN_EVIDENCE.template.json when it is one bounded issue under a frozen launch order (no wave, no forecast, no uncertainty register: report what you observed, do not author structure nobody decided -- #594); discrepancies remain evidence and MUST NOT be auto-filed as issues. Run python /home/tommy/.claude/skills/constellation-commander/scripts/verify_iterative_role_artifacts.py commander --work-id w3-ci; missing, malformed, or non-G2 run packets refuse execute completion. If a gate proves the plan wrong, surface the decision to the user before continuing. In delegated mode, surface a plan-invalidating discovery to the Admiral (float it) per the commander skill's Delegated/autonomous mode, rather than blocking on the human.

execute.context_headroom_note: #467. Absolute-token context reserve for THIS gate only: the engine subtracts it from both the soft and hard caps before dividing by the model's window, so `execute` may not be BEGUN with less than this much room left below the hard cap. It makes the imperative's existing prose instruction ('ensure context headroom before entering') enforceable, and it can only ever tighten -- no gate can raise a threshold. WHY 30000, and it is a GUESS, revisable in place: `execute` is the run's longest gate and the one that cannot be abandoned halfway, because it drives every crew gate and each crew dispatch costs tens of thousands of tokens. The only observation available was a commander sitting at ~127K fill after a cold resume plus one full three-task gate -- which bounds one gate's marginal cost in the tens of thousands but cannot separate it from the resume baseline. 30K is a round number at the low end of that range: on claude-opus-5 (1M window, 80K soft / 150K hard) it moves execute's begin-work line from 15% to 12% and its advisory from 8% to 5%, while every other gate keeps the shipped default. The named settle experiment (read fill_fraction across completed commander runs at the moment execute was started) is NOT runnable from existing artifacts -- gauge.json keeps only the latest reading and the per-gate context manifests record no fill -- so a later run may revise this number here, in this one place, without re-deriving anything.

feedback.title: Record workflow feedback
feedback.imperative: Before committing, reflect honestly on how this run actually went: how closely you followed the skills, handoffs, and checklists; where you had to improvise or work around the instructions; what was ambiguous, missing, or contradictory; and what would have helped. Include the crew Workflow Feedback harvested at each gN-integrate. A 'none' answer requires a run-specific reason ('none — confirmed after review: <what you checked>'); a bare 'none' does not close this step. Then record what happened as EPISODES: one episode per distinct thing that happened — not one per run, and not a summary — each stating its task-intent, expected-behavior, observed-behavior, impact-cost and workaround. An episode is a record, not a rule: write what you observed, and do NOT write a rule for a future agent to follow — a rule to follow belongs in docs/agents/* and is a human's call. Write the delta to .agent-work/w3-ci/episode-delta.json and apply it deterministically: python /home/tommy/.claude/skills/constellation-commander/scripts/apply_episode_delta.py --delta .agent-work/w3-ci/episode-delta.json --store-root episodes. Pass --store-root on every invocation: the writer's default resolves relative to the installed skill directory, so an installed copy would silently build a store at ~/.claude/skills/constellation-commander/episodes — outside the repo — while every gate reported green. Never hand-edit a file under episodes/: that writer is the only write path into it. Then run the capture gate before advancing: python /home/tommy/.claude/skills/constellation-commander/scripts/verify_episode_captured.py w3-ci --store-root episodes --phase feedback.

archive.title: Archive, commit, and push
archive.imperative: Commit all remaining work, including the episodes from this run under episodes/. That tracked repo-root path is the durable record. Push the branch and open its PR before the final lifecycle call, because c2 and c2b remain prerequisites on this Commander spine. Run the archive-phase capture gate before closing: python /home/tommy/.claude/skills/constellation-commander/scripts/verify_episode_captured.py w3-ci --store-root episodes --phase archive. Confirm the branch is clean and merge-ready. The engine mechanically refuses c4 when the staged diff includes suspicious artifacts; if an artifact is intentional, only a human may waive c4 through spine_evidence. Before closing, get the human's final acceptance of the archived run and record it as a fresh user-decision evidence item at THIS step -- satisfies c5. This is deliberately a second decision, not a re-read of review's run-summary evidence: the engine's artifact check only sees evidence attached to the current task, and issue #634's bookend freeze protects `archive` from `amend` precisely so the run's one human-acceptance gate cannot be dropped or rescoped out of a mutable middle step the way it could if it lived only at `review`. In delegated mode, satisfy c5 by attaching a user-decision evidence item citing the launch order (the spine_evidence tool with action=attach, task_id=archive, evidence_type=user-decision, fields={cite: 'LAUNCH_ORDER:Return Shape'}), the same section review already cites -- the Admiral ratifies, and the human ratifies at the epic return boundary. See the commander skill's Delegated/autonomous mode. Keep the engine lease active while you satisfy c1, c2, c2b, c3, c4, and c5. Attest c3 only when spine_close is the authorized sole final transition for this run. Then call spine_close once with why=<the final understanding>, tree_clean=true, episodes_captured=true, push=false, and open_pr=false. The false publication choices are deliberate because c2 and c2b already proved publication before this call. spine_close advances archive, releases declared child plans and the top-level lease, reaps bindings, and moves the work area into the archive in the existing finish_work order. Do not manually call the final spine_advance, spine_lease release, reap, or filesystem move. If spine_close refuses, fix the named readiness stage and retry the same tool; do not fall back to the retired manual sequence.

branch committed and pushed

the work is REACHABLE: this branch has a pull request that is OPEN or MERGED. A merged PR is reachable work; a closed-unmerged one is not, and neither is no PR at all. A terminal spine and a pushed branch describe the run, not the ref -- CI never runs on an unopened branch, and every commander that reached a terminal spine without opening one had to be chased for it. Open the PR even if the work is unfinished; declare FINAL or PENDING in its title and hand the merge up. Two properties of the check text are load-bearing. The branch is derived at CHECK time from the repo root, never resolved at instantiation: init instantiates the spine before it starts the branch, so the branch need not exist yet -- and a literal branch placeholder is not a resolver-owned token, so instantiation cannot catch one and would ship it unsubstituted. The count is compared in the SHELL because the engine's verdict for a command condition is the EXIT CODE and stdout is discarded: gh --jq 'length > 0' prints true or false but exits 0 either way, so that form can never fail.

check.command: test "$(gh pr list --head "$(git -C /home/tommy/projects/569-w3-ci rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)" --state all --json state --jq '[.[] | select(.state == "OPEN" or .state == "MERGED")] | length')" -gt 0
